links.outcome: Factual errors found by first-pass annotation versus multi-perspective adjudication in chatbot responses
links.effect: First-pass annotators frequently missed factual errors later validated by adjudicators; adjudicators also disagreed with each other, so multi-pass adjudication improves benchmark completeness but still needs judgment and expertise.
links.quote: First-pass annotators frequently miss factual errors later validated by adjudicators.

unlisted_practices: Using LLM-as-a-Judge to surface candidate factual errors alongside human annotation
Multi-source adjudication (medical-expert and evidence-based fact-checking) to improve hallucination benchmark completeness

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates methods for detecting factual errors and hallucinations in medical chatbot outputs, specifically testing multi-perspective adjudication and LLM-as-a-judge candidate discovery as safety/quality-control guardrail practices.
